description: Mistakes made, and what changed so they cannot recur. Every entry must name a concrete safeguard — a rule, a test, a check — not merely an intention to be careful.
why: A mistake that produces only an apology will happen again. A mistake that produces a test will not. This file is the audit trail of that conversion, and reading it is part of onboarding.
rules_for_this_file: Add an entry the moment an error is found, not later.
'safeguard' must be something executable or checkable. 'Be more careful' is not a safeguard.
Never delete an entry. A corrected mistake is still evidence of a weak spot.
If the same root cause appears twice, the safeguard was inadequate — say so and strengthen it.

lessons.title: Rent TDS deducted when none was due
lessons.what_happened: ₹3,000 was deducted under s.194I on rent of ₹30,000/month. The annual total (₹3,60,000) was compared against the ₹50,000 threshold, but that threshold is PER MONTH. ₹30,000/month is below it, so no TDS was ever due.
lessons.root_cause: Threshold basis was carried in prose, where per-month and per-year read alike.
lessons.cost: ₹3,000 wrongly withheld from the landlord, a challan filed under the wrong year, and a Q1 return that had to include a deduction that should not have existed.
lessons.safeguard: vm/rules/tds-in.json encodes threshold_basis explicitly ('per_month'). vm/rules/tds_engine.py refuses to compare a monthly-basis threshold against an annual total, and states in its explanation that 'annualised X is NOT the test'. Covered by a self-test case that fails if the behaviour regresses.

lessons.title: A vendor paid gross for four consecutive years
lessons.what_happened: Professional fees to the auditor were paid without TDS across FY2022-23 to FY2025-26 — roughly ₹4,71,000 of payments and ₹47,000 of undeducted TDS. Nobody was tracking the cumulative total per vendor.
lessons.root_cause: No monitoring. The rule was never in doubt; the running total was simply never computed.
lessons.cost: ~₹47,000 of TDS plus interest, spread across years now largely beyond correction.
lessons.safeguard: vm/rules/monitor.py computes year-to-date totals per vendor per section and flags 'breached-undeducted' and 'approaching' before the next payment. --check-payment answers 'what happens if I pay this?' BEFORE the money moves.
lessons.verified: monitor.py --check-payment on the live register returns the correct net-payable

lessons.title: Professional advice conflicted with the statute and was followed
lessons.what_happened: The firm's own tax team computed TDS of ₹12,500 plus ₹750 interest, then 73 minutes later withdrew it: 'tax is not deducted since the company already has significant accumulated losses'. Losses do not remove a deductor's liability under s.201 — they affect only the s.40(a)(ia) disallowance.
lessons.root_cause: Two distinct consequences of non-deduction were conflated, and the advice came from the party being paid.
lessons.cost: ₹12,500 plus accruing interest, and a fourth year added to the pattern in L002.
lessons.safeguard: tds-in.json records under 'penalty-non-deduction' that the 30% disallowance is a CONSEQUENCE of not deducting, never an alternative to it, and that the deductor remains liable under s.201 regardless of either party's losses. Roadmap phase 6 makes conflicts between advice and encoded rules visible rather than silently resolved.

lessons.title: The assistant asserted a fact it had not checked
lessons.what_happened: Asked which section a ₹980 default related to, the assistant answered 'rent TDS' by reasoning from a pattern seen in a different financial year. The bank statement showed no rent TDS in FY2024-25 at all. The operator asked 'are you sure? how did you find out?' and the claim collapsed.
lessons.root_cause: Pattern-matching substituted for retrieval, and the answer was stated with the same confidence as verified findings.
lessons.cost: None — caught immediately. Had it not been challenged, it would have driven a payment under the wrong section code.
lessons.safeguard: Two things. (1) Every answer about a fact must cite the document, bank line or voucher it came from; an uncited claim is a defect. (2) The coverage table (kb migration 003) makes 'I hold no evidence for that' an available and expected answer. Recorded in docs/compliance-safety-net.md as an explicit limit of the assistant, with the operator's challenge named as a control that works.
lessons.verified: docs/compliance-safety-net.md, section 'Four limits worth stating plainly', item 3

lessons.title: A migration recorded itself as applied when it had failed
lessons.what_happened: Migration 002 added a pgvector column. On a server without the extension it failed — but psql continued past the error and still inserted the schema_version row, so the schema history claimed a migration that had not run.
lessons.root_cause: psql continues after errors unless ON_ERROR_STOP is set, and the migration was not wrapped in a transaction.
lessons.cost: None in production; found during testing. Would have caused silent divergence between recorded and actual schema.
lessons.safeguard: Migrations run with -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1, migration 002 is wrapped in BEGIN/COMMIT so a failure rolls back its own version row, and kb-setup.ps1 re-queries schema_version after running rather than trusting the exit code.
lessons.verified: kb-setup.ps1 reports 'migration 002 skipped (needs pgvector)' and schema_version correctly omits version 2

lessons.title: Document classification silently ignored the project's own filenames
lessons.what_happened: Regex word boundaries (\b) treat _ and - as word characters, so '\bchallan\b' did not match '2026-05-07_challan.pdf' — exactly the naming convention ADR-0012 prescribes. Scanned documents with no extractable text were left unclassified and invisible to type filters.
lessons.root_cause: A regex assumption never tested against a real filename.
lessons.cost: 34 documents unfindable by type in a 291-document corpus. No external consequence, but the search would have quietly under-reported for months.
lessons.safeguard: Separators are normalised to spaces before matching, the filename is searched before the body, and vm/kb/test_ingest.py has a case asserting a scanned challan classifies from its filename alone.

lessons.title: Statement parser invented transactions from page furniture
lessons.what_happened: Loading a real FD statement produced 6 'transactions', two of which were not transactions at all: a printed timestamp ('Date And Time : 09/03/2026 12.44 PM') became a ₹12.44 line, and a 'Lien Balance: 0.00' footer became a zero-value line. Both contained a date and a decimal number, which was the only test applied.
lessons.root_cause: The parser accepted any line containing a date and a number. Statement footers and headers satisfy that trivially.
lessons.cost: None — caught on the first real run. But an invented transaction is the one parsing error that cannot be recovered by re-reading, because nothing downstream can tell it apart from a genuine one.
lessons.safeguard: vm/rules/reconcile.py adds NOISE_RE rejecting timestamps, balance/lien footers, page furniture and totals, plus a rule that at least one amount must be greater than zero. Every pattern in NOISE_RE comes from an observed false positive, and vm/rules/test_reconcile.py asserts both that the noise lines are rejected and that the real transactions on the same page still parse.

lessons.title: Statement loader reported 'no transactions' for a statement full of them
lessons.what_happened: A full-year statement containing hundreds of transactions parsed to zero. The PDF extracts as fragmented text with dates and amounts on separate lines ('TAX:0.8,080.00 5,31,763.'), which the line-based parser cannot match. It reported '0 transactions' and moved on.
lessons.root_cause: The parser had no way to distinguish 'this period had no activity' from 'I cannot read this layout', and reported both identically.
lessons.cost: None yet — caught in testing. In use it would have been worse than a crash: coverage would show the year as loaded, the evidence report would show 100% completeness, and a year of transactions would be invisible while every indicator said fine.
lessons.safeguard: vm/rules/reconcile.py adds diagnose_text(), which counts lines carrying dates versus amounts and names the actual cause — fragmented layout needing a table-aware extractor, a scan needing OCR, or an unsupported date format. The loader refuses to mark coverage 'held' when nothing parsed, so the year stays visibly 'missing'. Covered by test_reconcile.py::TestDiagnostics.
lessons.verified: test_reconcile.py::TestDiagnostics, and run against the real FY2025-26 statement: reports '306 lines have a date, 281 have an amount, but none have both'

lessons.title: Coordinate extractor looked successful while missing a third of the statement
lessons.what_happened: A coordinate-aware extractor pulled 240 transactions from a statement that line parsing could not read at all — every row dated, every row with an amount, descriptions correct, balances plausible. Cross-checking against three transactions known to be in that period found only one: the ₹1,47,500 ARTH audit fee and the ₹5,50,000 salary-arrears TDS were both absent, and only 9 of 12 monthly rent challans appeared.
lessons.root_cause: Two causes. The statement interleaves two accounts (current and FD) so a single running-balance chain does not apply; and the anchor heuristic requires a date and an amount in the movement column on the SAME visual row, which some layouts split differently. Neither was visible from internal consistency alone.
lessons.cost: None — caught before use. Had it been trusted, reconciliation would have reported clean exceptions while a third of the year's transactions were simply absent, and evidence completeness would have shown a high percentage against an incomplete population.
lessons.safeguard: vm/rules/pdf_table.py adds cross_check(), which verifies that transactions known to exist in a period were actually extracted, and the module docstring states plainly that balance continuity proves internal consistency but NOT completeness. The extractor is documented as ASSISTIVE — its output must be cross-checked against known transactions before any period is marked verified, and it does not mark coverage 'held' by itself.
lessons.verified: cross_check() against the FY2025-26 statement reports the two missing payments by name
